newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Assembly passes electronic toll legislation.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Assembly passes electronic toll legislation.

text.p: New Jersey drivers will soon be able to drive through a toll booth and signal "Charge it."
The state Assembly Monday passed a bill authorizing the state's three autonomous highway authorities to install the so-called EZ Pass system.

The system lets motorists install a plaque looking like a grocery-store bar code on their cars, which is read by a laser reader in the toll booth. The data are transmitted to a charge account, which the motorist pays monthly.
The cost to install the system will be nearly $500 million, and the award of the contract to MFS Network Technologies is being contested by Lockheed Martin.
The bill also authorizes the state to cooperate on interstate crossings, creating a non-stop network of highways from Connecticut to Maryland.
Participating highways in New Jersey are the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway and the Atlantic City Expressway.
